narrative.weekly_mirror: You noticed moments that could have brought enjoyment—a long bath with lavender salts, a massage, or lying down with a heat pad—but they kept being displaced by cleaning, the next task, or an inherited warning about being “pampered.” This also echoes the missed CNY market with Mei and Hwee Leng, even alongside the pleasure of pandan chiffon cake and hot Milo before anyone else was up.
narrative.tension_explanation: This week, enjoying life and having fun appears to have been repeatedly set aside when other responsibilities or self-denying expectations came forward. The tension is especially clear in “Everything becomes about what needs doing next” and in hearing your mother’s voice when you considered rest; it remains unclear how much choice felt available in those moments.
narrative.reflective_question: When you look at the bath, massage, heat pad, and CNY market together, what do you notice about what makes enjoyment feel possible or difficult to claim?
